subject: maths
card: Number bonds, clever ways to add and subtract in your head, doubling, halving and estimating.
title: Mental maths
seo_title: Mental maths strategies and practice (KS2, ages 9 to 11)
description: Mental maths strategies explained simply: number bonds to 10, 100 and 1,000, adding and subtracting in your head, doubling and halving, multiplying by 5, 20 and 25, and estimating answers. Free practice with hints for ages 9 to 11.
intro: You don't need a pencil for everything! Learn a few clever tricks and you can work out lots of sums in your head, and check your written answers too.

units.title: Number bonds to 10, 100 and 1,000
units.blurb: Pairs that make a round number.

learn.p: Pairs of whole numbers that add up to 10: 1 + 9, 2 + 8, 3 + 7, 4 + 6, 5 + 5. Knowing these by heart makes everything else quicker.

Use your bonds to 10 for the tens, then make the ones up to a full ten. 64 + ? = 100: 64 needs 6 to get to 70, and then 30 to get to 100. So 64 + 36 = 100. Check: the ones (4 + 6) make 10 and the tens (6 + 3) make 9.
For multiples of 10 it works the same way: 370 + 630 = 1,000, because 37 + 63 = 100.

questions.hint: 45 needs 5 to get to 50. Then how many to get to 100?
What goes with 28 to make 100? 28 needs 2 to get to 30…
25 + ? = 100. Then make it ten times bigger.
3 tenths + how many tenths make 10 tenths?

questions.q: You have 100p. You spend 63p. How much change do you get?

units.title: Adding in your head
units.blurb: Split numbers up, and use near tens.

learn.p: 47 + 36: add the tens, 40 + 30 = 70. Add the ones, 7 + 6 = 13. Then 70 + 13 = 83.
To add 9, add 10 then take 1 away. 56 + 9 = 66 − 1 = 65. To add 29, add 30 and take 1 away: 47 + 29 = 77 − 1 = 76.
With lots of numbers, look for pairs that make a ten first. 6 + 7 + 4 + 3: (6 + 4) + (7 + 3) = 10 + 10 = 20.

units.title: Subtracting in your head
units.blurb: Count on, or take away a near ten.

learn.p: To take away 9, take away 10 and add 1 back. 73 − 9 = 63 + 1 = 64. To take away 19: 73 − 20 = 53, then add 1 back: 54.

learn.h: Count on to find the difference
learn.p: When the numbers are close, count on from the smaller one. 403 − 396: from 396 to 400 is 4, then to 403 is 3 more. The difference is 7.
Subtraction and addition undo each other. If 82 − 47 = 35, then 35 + 47 should be 82. It is, so the answer is right.

questions.hint: The numbers are close. Count on from 497.

questions.q: Mia says 73 − 38 = 45. How can she check?
options: Work out 45 + 38 and see if it makes 73
questions.explain: If 73 − 38 = 45 then 45 + 38 should be 73. But 45 + 38 = 83, so Mia is wrong. The right answer is 35.

questions.q: A book has 120 pages. Sam has read 85. How many pages are left?

units.title: Doubling and halving
units.blurb: Two tricks that unlock lots of other sums.

learn.p: Half of 58: half of 50 is 25, half of 8 is 4. 25 + 4 = 29. For an odd tens number like 70, think: half of 70 is 35, because 35 + 35 = 70.
In a times sum you can double one number and halve the other, and the answer stays the same. 16 × 5 = 8 × 10 = 80. 14 × 25 = 7 × 50 = 350.

questions.hint: Half of 70 is 35. Half of 6 is 3.
Half of 100 is 50, half of 30 is 15.

units.title: Multiplying and dividing in your head

learn.p: × 5 is the same as × 10 then halve: 46 × 5 = 460 ÷ 2 = 230. × 25 is the same as × 100 then divide by 4: 12 × 25 = 1,200 ÷ 4 = 300.
23 × 4: split 23 into 20 and 3. 20 × 4 = 80 and 3 × 4 = 12. 80 + 12 = 92. To divide, split into numbers that divide easily: 72 ÷ 3 = (60 ÷ 3) + (12 ÷ 3) = 20 + 4 = 24.

questions.explain: Half of 84 is 42, half of 42 is 21.

questions.q: Cinema tickets cost £5 each. How many pounds do 36 tickets cost?

units.title: Estimating and checking
units.blurb: Round first to see if an answer makes sense.

learn.p: To estimate 398 + 214, round each number: 400 + 200 = 600. The real answer (612) should be close to 600.
If someone says 48 × 21 = 108, estimate: 50 × 20 = 1,000. 108 is much too small, so it must be wrong. (It's 1,008.)
Shopping: £2.95 + £4.10 + £1.99 is about £3 + £4 + £2 = £9. Handy for checking you have enough money!

questions.q: Which is the best estimate for 504 + 297?
questions.hint: Round each number to the nearest 100.

questions.q: Which is the best estimate for 31 × 19?

options: No: the answer should be about 200
No: the answer should be about 1,000
questions.explain: 600 − 400 = 200, so 323 is too big. The exact answer is 223.

questions.q: Which is the best estimate for 4.9 × 6.1?
questions.hint: Round each to the nearest whole number.

questions.q: You buy three things that cost £1.95, £3.05 and £0.99. About how much is that altogether?
questions.hint: Round each price to the nearest pound.

questions.q: Which is the best estimate for 798 ÷ 4?
